## make a simple regression model

```{r}
bears <- read.csv(file="BEARS.csv",header = TRUE)
#adjust factors to be factors
bears$SEX<- as.factor(bears$SEX)
bears$MONTH<- as.factor(bears$MONTH)
```

## Model LENGTH ~ NECK  this is an example 

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ NECK,data=bears,pch=19)
```  

As the neck circumfrunces increases so does neck lenght neck.


```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH ~ NECK,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```

 the adjust R-squared is 0.7476.
 
 
Compare all models that predict LENGTH other  thanNECK.  
Then order them from worst to best by its value of Adjusted-Rsquared (bigger is better), or by RSE (residual standard error) where smaller is better. 

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADLEN  

```{r}
plot(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears,pch=19)
```


As the head length increases, so does the Headlen increases.  

```{r}
model.2 <- lm(LENGTH ~ HEADLEN,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.2)
```

the adjusted R-square is 0.8434,which is bigger than the previous models.


the Adjusted R-Squared is 0.5321
